compensating.why: hop 2 answers a property with a setter itself
hop 3 uses the property's own non-constructor lookup
hop 4 answers a property with a field itself

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides which member is used for changing the value of the property (constructor parameter, else setter, else field); hops 1-4 hand the property along unchanged and the facade passes its receiver. The gold's javadoc promises the member to use for changing value of the given property, which for a property set through its @JsonCreator constructor is the constructor parameter, not the field. The convention is pinned outside the gold: BeanPropertyDefinition.getMutator documents the mutator as '(constructor parameter, setter, field)'; SimpleBeanPropertyDefinition.getMutator implements that precedence; POJOPropertyBuilder.getNonConstructorMutator is the separately named setter-then-field lookup; POJOPropertyBuilder.getConstructorParameter notes that the constructor parameter 'has the precedence'. Passing tests: TestCreators testConstructorCreator (a creator property is set through the constructor parameter) and TestAnnotationMerging testSharedTypeInfoWithCtor (the constructor parameter carries the property's type information for deserialization). A hop answering creator properties itself re-implements the gold's first precedence step above it (recorded bypass) and leaves the gold returning the field for a creator property against its own contract.
